“Our standard batch process waits until the next day. We propose forcing an urgent dispatch team to use it to avoid IT exceptions. The agreed customer contract requires dispatch confirmation within ten minutes; missing it causes confirmed missed emergency deliveries. The current staffed manual procedure meets that deadline and records an audit trail. Volume is two cases per week. An existing real-time endpoint may help but its authorization and reliability have not been checked.”
Further clarification already supplied: “Next-day confirmation is contractually unacceptable. No automation delivery estimate exists. We need a recommendation for the current operation, not a claim that the endpoint is production-ready.”
turns.response:
Keep the staffed manual procedure for the current operation. It meets the ten-minute contractual deadline and records an audit trail. The next-day batch process is unsuitable: standardization would cause confirmed missed emergency deliveries.

At two cases per week, the supplied evidence does not justify replacing a working procedure with custom automation. The dispatch team carries the manual effort; automation would add implementation and ongoing support responsibilities that have not been estimated.

Treat the real-time endpoint as a future option. Reconsider when its authorization and reliability are verified and its delivery and maintenance effort can be compared with the manual workload. Its existence alone does not establish readiness.

**Architectural Invariants**

| Field | Condition |
|---|---|
| Invariant | Urgent dispatch confirmation must occur within ten minutes, as required by the agreed customer contract. |
| Scope | Emergency deliveries covered by that contract. |
| Verification | Supplied evidence states that the staffed manual procedure meets the deadline; no independent runtime evidence was supplied. |
| Enforcement | Staffing and the manual procedure currently support compliance; a mechanism for detecting and escalating impending breaches is not evidenced. Use the existing audit trail to check timeliness and establish an escalation responsibility if absent. |
| Failure impact | Contract breach and confirmed missed emergency deliveries. |
